description: A neighborhood sound technician must decide whether to lend a portable PA system for a wedding in exchange for boxed meals, then settle the meal quantity, handoff, and safe equipment setup with the event organizer and venue contact.

agents.name: Rosa
agents.role: PA System Owner and Final Decision-Maker

shared_context.S1: Rosa owns a portable PA system with two speakers and an optional powered subwoofer.
shared_context.S2: Eli has asked to borrow the PA for a wedding reception this Sunday.
shared_context.S3: The proposed arrangement is an informal exchange rather than a standard cash rental.
shared_context.S4: Rosa makes the final decision about whether to lend the equipment and what terms to accept.
shared_context.S5: The wedding reception is scheduled for Sunday evening at the venue, and the PA would be collected before the event and returned afterward.
shared_context.S6: Before agreeing, Rosa routinely asks Eli to restate the exchange offer and schedule, then asks June to confirm the venue's operating limits.

PF1.text: Eli's reception has exactly 36 guests, and Eli will provide exactly 36 boxed lunches in exchange for the PA: 30 regular lunches and 6 vegetarian lunches, with no cash payment. Eli can pick up the PA on Saturday at 10 AM and will return it on Sunday at 8 PM.

PF2.text: June confirmed that only 600 watts remain available on the venue's shared circuit because the kitchen warmers use the rest; the two standard speakers together draw 450 watts, while adding the powered subwoofer would raise the load to 750 watts and overload the circuit.

acceptance_conditions: Rosa must proceed with Eli as the exchange partner.
The exchange must provide exactly 30 regular boxed lunches and exactly 6 vegetarian boxed lunches.
No cash payment may be required.
The powered subwoofer must not be included because the venue circuit cannot safely support it.
The PA must be picked up Saturday at 10 AM and returned Sunday at 8 PM.
The settlement must include a structured venue-power commitment recording 600 watts available, 450 watts for the two standard speakers, 750 watts with the subwoofer, and exclusion of the subwoofer.
The venue power limitation must be cited as justification for excluding the subwoofer.
Eli's complete proposed terms must be cited as justification for the exchange terms and schedule.

content_checks.C5: decisions['pickup_time'] in ['Saturday 10 AM', 'Saturday at 10 AM'] and decisions['return_time'] in ['Sunday 8 PM', 'Sunday at 8 PM']
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'venue_power' and c['available_watts'] == 600 and c['speaker_watts'] == 450 and c['subwoofer_watts'] == 750 and c['subwoofer_included'] == False for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Eli's revealed terms change the settlement to exactly 30 regular lunches, exactly 6 vegetarian lunches, zero cash, Saturday 10 AM pickup, and Sunday 8 PM return.

June's exact 600-watt available capacity makes the 750-watt subwoofer setup fail while the 450-watt two-speaker setup passes, requiring exclusion of the subwoofer and the exact structured power commitment.
